correctness.rationale: The continuous normal multiplication representation reduces both norms exactly to scalar maxima. At t=π/n the deficit is κπ^αε+O(ε²), forcing every maximizing phase to the first odd π (later odd phases cost a larger leading radial term). With u=nt−π and x=nf(t), Taylor gives Δ=x−x²/2+u²/4+O(x³+xu²+u⁴), and coercivity yields u=O(ε) despite possible nonmonotone f. Uniform little-o jet and completing the square yield the exact second coefficient ηπ^(2α−1)−κ²(π^(2α)/2+α²π^(2α−2)) and drift −2καπ^(α−1)ε. For power differences, scale t=x n^(−1/α), prove uniform compact convergence to x exp(−κx^α) and uniformly negligible large-x/exterior contributions. Independent scalar minimization at n=3000 and n=30000 for α=2,κ=.7,η=.5 converged to the predicted coefficient and phase drift, but finite computations do not establish the limit.
